finding.evidence: error text differs for a valid username; 50 attempts in 10 s accepted
finding.description: Usernames can be enumerated and passwords brute-forced.

recommendation.goal: What is the recommended fix for this web security flaw: weak-authentication (Usernames can be enumerated and passwords brute-forced. Evidence: error text differs for a valid username; 50 attempts in 10 s accepted). State the concrete fix and cite a primary source (OWASP, MDN, NIST, PCI DSS, IETF RFC, or the vendor's own advisory).
recommendation.answer: Fix: return same generic 'invalid username or password' for all failures to prevent enumeration; enforce rate limiting plus account lockout to restrict excessive authentication attempts and mitigate brute-force/password-guessing; log all authentication failures and alert administrators when credential stuffing or brute force is detected.

sources.contribution: Use generic Authentication and Error Messages that do not reveal valid usernames
Account lockout mechanisms are used to mitigate brute force attacks
Log all failures and alert administrators when credential stuffing, brute force, or other attacks are detected or suspected

fix.summary: Return generic login error and enforce 5-failures-per-minute lockout with failure logging.
fix.risk: Legitimate admin is locked out for 10 minutes after 5 failed attempts.
